description: Core per-character combat stats: health, guard durability, down value and the timing constants that initialize the status controller.

Id.simple: Character ID used as the row key.
Id.technical: Unreal DataTable row name. ResolveDataRows resolves it from CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterBaseParameter or the studio BaseParameterIdOverride and treats a miss as fatal; several UI phases resolve the same row directly from CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterBaseParameter. The export has 122 rows.

HitPoint.simple: Base maximum health for team play.
HitPoint.technical: Float health units. ApplyHitPointParameters uses HitPoint unless FGameCharacterStatusSetup.SoloSide == 1 (then HitPoint_Solo) and no positive HitPointOverride is set; it initializes HitPointMax and current HitPoint. GamePvESettings also falls back to this column for a character with no explicit HitPoint when not in solo.

HitPoint_Solo.technical: Selected instead of HitPoint when Setup.SoloSide == 1 in ApplyHitPointParameters and in the GamePvESettings fallback. Setup.HitPointOverride still takes priority. CP_010 exports the same value as HitPoint (440).

AttackRange.simple: Serialized attack-range value; no direct consumer was found.
AttackRange.technical: Float at row offset 0x18, exported 1250.0 for CP_010. No Source/Plugins consumer reads CharacterBaseParameterRow.AttackRange; distance gating in the reconstructed code uses AttackSet.AttackRangeType and action controller flags instead. The field's practical meaning is unresolved from available evidence.

Guard_Minimum_Time.simple: Minimum time a guard must be held before certain guard transitions.
Guard_Minimum_Time.technical: Seconds. Guard action code tests Elapsed > Guard_Minimum_Time together with GuardRigidityTime <= 0.0f; CP_180's guard behavior uses the same predicate. At or below this time the relevant guard transition is blocked.

GuardDurability.simple: Base guard gauge that depletes when hits are blocked.
GuardDurability.technical: Float. UpdateGuardDurability copies it into GuardDurabilityBase and initializes CurrentGuardDurability as GetGuardDurabilityMaxRate() * GuardDurability. AI value conditions divide current durability by this row value, and guard-hit effects use NewHitPoint / this value to choose an effect.

GuardDurability_Solo.simple: Serialized solo guard-durability value; no direct consumer was found.
GuardDurability_Solo.technical: Float at row offset 0x24 (CP_010 exports 150.0, equal to GuardDurability). UpdateGuardDurability only reads GuardDurability in this source snapshot; no solo-side substitution for durability is present. The rebuilt guard regeneration path likewise uses the shared BaseParameterRow->GuardDurability_Recover. Treat the solo override as unimplemented/unidentified rather than proven used.

GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime.simple: Serialized delay before guard durability regenerates; no direct consumer was found.
GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime.technical: Float at row offset 0x28 (CP_010 exports 3.0 seconds by name/value convention). The current Tick implementation gates regeneration only with bGuardDurabilityRegenEnabled / bGuardDurabilityRegenBlocked and reads GuardDurability_Recover; no read of GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime exists in Source/Plugins. This is a serialized-but-unconsumed field in the reconstruction.

GuardDurability_Recover.simple: Rate at which guard durability regenerates.
GuardDurability_Recover.technical: Float denominator in (100.0 / Recover) * DeltaTime: smaller values regenerate faster. With regeneration enabled and unblocked, below the rate-scaled maximum and Recover > 0, the tick adds that amount to CurrentGuardDurability and clamps to the scaled maximum. CP_010 exports 15.0.

DownValue.simple: Down gauge: stamina-like value depleted by blows before a character is knocked down.
DownValue.technical: Float. ApplyDownValueParameters copies it to DownValueMax and current DownValue; ResetDownValue also uses it for adaptation values and max(HitPoint - DownValue, 0). Damage handling subtracts down damage scaled by the receiver's down-damage rate, and AI conditions inspect DownValue / DownValueMax. Many later DownValue hits are status-controller fields, not row reads.

LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime.simple: Down-gauge recovery delay for large characters.
LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime.technical: Seconds. RestartDownValueRecover chooses this row value when GetActionSlot146() flags a large character; otherwise it uses Global.DownValue_Recover_Time. CN_240 adaptation also begins with this duration. CP_010 exports 0.0, so large-character recovery is effectively immediate for that row.

notes: Three fields (AttackRange, GuardDurability_Solo, GuardDurability_RecoverWaitTime) are serialized with verified retail offsets but have no identifiable C++ consumer in this snapshot; their gameplay meaning is not asserted.
The solo flag is FGameCharacterStatusSetup.SoloSide == 1. Only HitPoint/HitPoint_Solo have an observed solo substitution in the available code.
The exported table has 122 rows; available Content is partial, so exported values do not characterize every retail character.
All consumer descriptions come from reconstructed source; layout-check references confirm field presence/offset only, not behavior or byte-match.

usages.detail: Resolves the required BaseParameter row during character setup (override id wins over CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterBaseParameter).
Uses HitPoint/HitPoint_Solo to initialize maximum and current health, unless an explicit setup override is present.
Uses DownValue to initialize the down gauge and its maximum.
Uses GuardDurability to initialize GuardDurabilityBase and CurrentGuardDurability with the battle rate multiplier.
Blocks the guard transition until Guard_Minimum_Time has elapsed and rigidity has ended.
Uses GuardDurability_Recover as the regeneration-rate denominator.
Selects LargeCharacterDownRecoverTime for large-character down recovery instead of the Global row's time.
Falls back to the row's HitPoint/HitPoint_Solo for PvE settings when a character has no explicit health.
Reads the same row for versus-enemy character settings UI.
